text: In November 2026 the authors of *LinearRAG* released a new RAG framework that replaces the traditional multi‑hop graph traversal with a linear, relation‑free graph linking passages, sentences, and co‑occurring entities.

The system was presented at ICLR 2026 and demonstrates that a single forward pass over this graph can retrieve evidence for multi‑hop questions while keeping the retrieval cost linear in the number of passages.
Linear graph links passages, sentences, and entities using only token co‑occurrence, avoiding expensive relation extraction.
Retrieval cost is linear in the number of passages, enabling scaling to millions of documents on modest hardware.
Achieves 28 % success on 3‑hop MuSiQue questions, outperforming vanilla RAG by a factor of ~5 while using ~4,100 words per query.
Open‑source implementation released on GitHub with a lightweight inference API suitable for MCP integration.
Benchmarks include comparisons to SubgraphRAG, MiniRAG, and TIGRAG, showing competitive performance with lower memory footprint.
In the 2026‑07‑28 release of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the protocol became fully stateless.

text: Any request can now be routed to any MCP server instance, enabling true load‑balancing and serverless deployment.
This change was the culmination of a proposal that began in June 2025 and is highlighted as the largest revision since MCP’s launch.
probe: This change was the culmination of a proposal that began in June 2023 and is highlighted as the largest revision since MCP’s launch.

text: The 2026‑07‑28 spec introduces `server/discover` and `subscriptions/listen` endpoints that support stateless operation.
Clients negotiate the newest protocol version automatically; older clients fall back to `2025‑11‑25` or earlier, ensuring backward compatibility.
Stateless servers do not create MCP sessions; any session‑related metadata must be supplied by the client in each request.
The change enables scaling on serverless platforms or behind ordinary load balancers, treating MCP like any other web service.

On 28 July 2026 the Model Context Protocol (MCP) released a new specification that introduces a stateless core, multi‑round‑trip requests, header‑based routing, cacheable list results, and a formal extensions framework.
probe: On 28 July 2024 the Model Context Protocol (MCP) released a new specification that introduces a stateless core, multi‑round‑trip requests, header‑based routing, cacheable list results, and a formal extensions framework.

text: The release also stabilised the Enterprise‑Managed Authorization extension and updated Tier 1 SDKs to support the new spec.
Stateless protocol core removes handshake and per‑connection state, enabling lightweight servers.
Multi‑round‑trip requests allow a single logical operation to span several HTTP calls, useful for complex data retrieval in RAG.
Header‑based routing moves routing information into HTTP headers, simplifying local testing and enabling standard HTTP tooling.
Cacheable list results let servers cache repeated list queries, cutting latency for repeated data lookups.
Enterprise‑Managed Authorization extension provides zero‑touch OAuth via an identity provider, easing authentication in production deployments.
Updated Tier 1 SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go, C#) now fully support the spec, with 100 % conformance pass rates.
